newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna bourse aims to dampen closing price swings.
newsitem.headline: Vienna bourse aims to dampen closing price swings.

text.p: Vienna stock exchange said on Friday it planned to introduce a weighted close for ATX shares and raise the minimum trading volume for market makers in order to reduce the risk of big price movements in late trade.

In a statement, the Vienna bourse said the move was in response to a late sell-off on October 16 which pushed the ATX index of blue-chip shares down to 1,073.54 points from 1,089 just prior to the close.
"For the future we plan to calculate and publish a weighted average for each continuously traded share. Investors can use it as a basis for their portfolios and positions," the Vienna bourse said.
"At the same time the minimum trading volume for market makers will be increased. In the next few days we will seek the agreement of market makers," it continued.
Traders forecast the minimum trading volume would rise to 1,000 lots from 500 at present.

They traced Wednesday's 1.38 percent decline in the ATX during the last few minutes of trade to a battle between two Austrian banks. "One was trying to buy the market up and the other was trying to sell it down," a trader said.
Selling pressure centred on ATX heavyweights oil group OMV, insurer EA-Generali and steel firm VA Stahl, traders said.
EA-Generali ended 5.6 percent down on October 16, VA Stahl 5.5 percent down and OMV four percent down.
